title: Set the Rules for Data Centres
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Welcome data centres and AI infrastructure where they benefit Victoria—but make major facilities carry the additional power, water, infrastructure and environmental costs they create, and subject them to transparent assessment and genuine community consultation.

title: Turn Trams into Surface Rapid Transit
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Upgrade Melbourne’s strongest tram corridors as surface rapid transit: physically separate trams from general traffic where feasible, give them stronger signal priority, build safe level-access platforms, run frequent all-day services, coordinate feeder buses and close short missing links to rail and major centres where the business case supports them.

title: Deliver Accessible Public Transport
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Turn Victoria’s known public-transport accessibility backlog into a funded construction program. Publish every non-compliant stop and station, set delivery dates, and stop commissioning broad studies where the barrier and remedy are already understood.

title: Open Government by Default
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Reignite democracy through proactive disclosure: publish government information before people have to FOI it, and make meetings, contracts, decisions and representative access easier to see and scrutinise.

title: Protect Whistleblowers
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Strengthen Victoria's existing public-interest disclosure system so people can report serious wrongdoing without being destroyed by retaliation or procedural traps.

title: Police Integrity and Independent Accountability
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Pair effective policing with genuinely independent misconduct oversight, transparent use-of-power data, strong civil-liberties safeguards and procedural fairness.

title: Complete Neighbourhoods
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Stop approving dormitory suburbs that lock residents into driving for basic daily life. New growth areas should permit local shops and services, provide safe access to daily needs, and have useful public transport operating as homes are occupied.

title: Prevention First Public Safety
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Make preventing victimisation a core public-safety function: safer places, earlier support, targeted problem-solving, proportionate intervention and independent evaluation.

title: Problem-Oriented Policing
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Concentrate policing and prevention on demonstrated local harms, micro-locations and repeat problems rather than indiscriminate enforcement.

title: Safer Night-Time Precincts
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Treat late-night violence as a precinct problem involving transport, venue management, lighting, crowd movement, health services and targeted policing.

title: Youth Diversion and Early Intervention
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Expand early support and consistent diversion for suitable low-level youth offending, while keeping serious violence on a separate risk and victim-safety pathway.

title: Neighbourhood Police Posts
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Trial neighbourhood police posts staffed by familiar, fully sworn but ordinarily unarmed community officers in lighter uniforms, with voluntary universal introductions, local patrols, independent oversight and civil-liberties safeguards.

title: Homes and Stations Code
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Allow duplexes, terraces, small apartments and local shops across serviced suburbs, and treat every major station as the centre of a mixed-use neighbourhood rather than an isolated transport node.

title: No Single Points of Failure
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Melbourne's rail network has no redundancy: when a single Telstra network fault halted every V/Line train in the state on 8 July 2026, there was no backup for passengers to fall back on. Singapore runs three separate lines through its busiest corridor for exactly this reason. Legislate a redundancy standard for new transit investment, and apply the same principle to bus corridors by pairing route staggering with built-in route overlap.

title: Finish the Network
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Build the missing rail links as a network, not as isolated projects: electrify overdue growth corridors, create genuinely new orbital coverage in the west, and put stations where they can anchor real neighbourhood centres.

title: End FlexiRide's Fake Flexibility
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: FlexiRide and similar on-demand services currently require hours of lead time and can still drop passengers hundreds of metres short of their actual destination. Legislate minimum service standards for on-demand transit: maximum booking lead time, and door-to-door rather than zone-to-zone delivery.

title: Fix the Order, Not Just the Fare
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Improve coverage, frequency and reliability before considering fare-free travel. Publish the service and fare trade-offs.

title: Connect the Regions
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Victoria's regional network is built entirely hub-and-spoke through Melbourne. A Ballarat resident travelling to Bendigo has to route via the city despite the two being roughly 100km apart directly. Commission a direct regional cross-connectivity study for major regional-to-regional pairs currently requiring a Melbourne detour.

title: Set a Transit Access Standard
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Set and publish a statewide public-transport access standard based on real walking distance, service frequency and span—not a nominal stop within an arbitrary radius.

title: Stagger the Timetables
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Where two bus routes share a corridor, DTP frequently schedules them to arrive at the same time instead of staggered, halving effective frequency for free. Mandate a statewide audit and correction of every shared-corridor timetable clash.

title: Nothing Without the People
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Create a safeguarded citizen-initiative process for major democratic and constitutional questions, beginning with deliberation and advisory votes rather than an unrestricted popular veto over ordinary legislation.

title: Communities Set Policy
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Give communities direct control over a defined share of discretionary local public investment through participatory budgeting—without creating a local veto over housing, land use or statewide infrastructure.

title: Citizens in Every Room
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Use representative citizens’ panels for major, genuinely contested long-term questions to improve deliberation and scrutiny—without creating a parallel legislature or another veto point for routine housing and infrastructure delivery.

title: Expose Hidden Campaign Labour
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Require parties and candidates to disclose material paid, seconded and professionally supplied campaign labour that would otherwise hide outside ordinary donation reporting—without forcing genuine grassroots volunteers to keep political timesheets.

title: End Cash-for-Access Politics
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: End political fundraising models that sell private access to ministers, MPs or candidates. Require paid political-access events and material policy discussions to be transparent, while preserving ordinary fundraising and open engagement with businesses, unions, community groups and citizens.

title: Expose Preference Deal Money
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Victoria abolished group voting tickets for Legislative Council elections in August 2026. Voters now direct at least five preferences above or below the line. Disclose any money or in-kind support tied to preference recommendations and how-to-vote deals.

title: Fund the Outer Suburbs
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Create a transparent growth-area infrastructure program that directs transport and local infrastructure funding to documented service gaps, population growth and project value—not an arbitrary geographic quota.

title: Fix Transit Deserts
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Build a high-frequency outer-suburban bus grid now, while planning rail and activity centres so fast-growing suburbs are not permanently locked into car dependence.

title: Build the Melton Line
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Quadruplicate the rail corridor between Melton and Sunshine to give Melton its own dedicated, electrified metro line, instead of sharing track with V/Line's diesel regional services to Ballarat, to match the pace of growth in Melbourne's outer west.

title: Take Back Public Assets
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Keep strategic public assets and their returns in public hands. Audit expiring operating contracts and test public provision against regulated alternatives before selecting an operator.

title: Build Housing at Stations
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Build and retain public homes on strategic station land, and make station precincts real neighbourhood centres with homes, shops, services and jobs—not isolated platforms surrounded by parking or single-use zoning.

title: Charge the Car Parks
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Levy a commercial parking station tax in inner-urban areas to discourage peak-hour driving and fund public transit.

title: Unmask Transurban's Discount
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Investigate the secret toll discounts and concessions granted to Transurban across the metropolitan road network.

title: Audit Southern Cross
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Conduct a full operational and financial audit of the Southern Cross Station public-private partnership.

title: Expose the Tunnel Deal
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Declassify and publish all secret toll road contracts and traffic volume guarantees in full.

title: Pay Every Victorian
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Distribute a Citizens Dividend to all Victorians financed by the returns of the Sovereign Wealth Fund.

title: Build the Sovereign Fund
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Establish a Victorian Sovereign Wealth Fund powered by resource royalties and land value taxes to build long-term generational wealth.

title: Tax the Land Windfalls
author: not exported
summary_verbatim:
Victoria already has a Windfall Gains Tax: up to 50% on rezoning uplift, with a 62.5% marginal rate in the $100,000–$500,000 taper band. 

The problem is where the money goes. 

It flows into consolidated revenue and disappears. 

We'll legislate to redirect it into a ring-fenced Transit Capital Fund, so that the value created by public infrastructure decisions is reinvested in public infrastructure.

title: Claw Back Franchise Profits
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Audit transport franchises. Compare public and regulated operators before each contract decision, while keeping one integrated passenger network.

title: Audit the Fake Surplus
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Victoria extended the public lottery licence for 40 years in return for a $1.145 billion upfront premium. VAGO found no significant probity issues, but identified transparency limits and said further sensitivity testing would have strengthened the valuation evidence. We want the long-term value-for-money case on the public record.

title: Smooth the Pension Cliff
author: not exported
summary_verbatim: Examine whether a longer repayment schedule for Victoria's defined-benefit superannuation liabilities would improve cash flow without increasing long-run risk. Publish actuarial and legal advice before proposing a timetable.
